coverage_note: State and local public employees under the Public Employees' Fair Employment Act (the Taylor Law), Civil Service Law article 14 (sections 200 to 215), administered by PERB or a local 'mini-PERB'. The official statute text on nysenate.gov sits behind a Cloudflare challenge that refused the capture agent (HTTP 403), and its API requires a key, so the cells quote PERB's own guide to the Taylor Law (twelfth edition, revised September 2025) and PERB's rules. Statutory section numbers come from those PERB documents where they give them; otherwise the cell cites the PERB document.
quote_normalization: quote_binding exact-substring is checked after Unicode NFC and collapsing every run of whitespace (including no-break space) to one space, in both the quote and the text extracted from the captured bytes (HTML: BeautifulSoup get_text; PDF: pdftotext)
provenance_id_canonicalization: provenance_id = 'prov-' + sha256 of the record serialized as JSON with sorted keys, separators (',', ':'), UTF-8, without the provenance_id field; re-fingerprint with scripts/lib/provenance.mjs once P0 lands
disclaimer: Reference summary of public law, not legal advice. Members with a specific case should talk to a steward or a lawyer.

governing_statute.value: Public Employees' Fair Employment Act (Taylor Law), N.Y. Civil Service Law sections 200 to 215
governing_statute.quote: The Taylor Law grants public employees the right to form, join and participate in, or to refrain from forming, joining or participating in, an employee organization of their choice, and the right to have an employee organization negotiate with their employer to determine their terms and conditions of employment
governing_statute.pinpoint: PERB, What Is the Taylor Law?, part V

who_may_bargain.value: Public employees of the State and its subdivisions, except employees designated managerial or confidential and the specific positions the law excludes
who_may_bargain.quote: A confidential employee is one who acts and assists in a confidential capacity to a managerial employee who is involved in labor relations, personnel or contract administration. In addition, the Taylor Law defines certain specific positions as managerial or confidential.

scope_of_bargaining.quote: requires public employers to negotiate and enter into agreements with public employee organizations regarding their employees’ terms and conditions of employment

impasse_procedure.value: Parties may agree on their own procedures; otherwise PERB mediation, then fact-finding, then (except school districts and arbitration-eligible units) a legislative determination binding for up to one year. Police, firefighters, certain transit employees, state police and some others have compulsory binding interest arbitration.
impasse_procedure.quote: In impasses involving police, firefighter, certain transit employees, the state police, state security services and law enforcement personnel and deputy sheriffs who are police officers engaged in law enforcement more than half of the time, the Law authorizes compulsory interest arbitration, by which one party may seek to compel arbitration of the dispute.
impasse_procedure.pinpoint: PERB, What Is the Taylor Law?, part V (Resolution of Contract Disputes)

strike_legality.value: Prohibited. Strikers lose two days' pay for each strike day, and employee organizations may not cause, instigate, encourage or condone a strike.
strike_legality.quote: The Taylor Law continues the common law prohibition against strikes in the public sector. Employee organizations may not cause, instigate, encourage, or condone a strike.
strike_legality.pinpoint: PERB, What Is the Taylor Law?, part VIII (Civil Service Law section 210)

agency_fee_status.value: Not collectible from nonconsenting public employees under Janus v. AFSCME (2018). PERB's guide still lists forfeiture of 'agency fee check-off privileges' among strike penalties, reflecting older statute text.
agency_fee_status.quote: For these reasons, States and public-sector unions may no longer extract agency fees from nonconsenting employees.

dfr_forum.value: PERB. Breaching the duty of fair representation is an employee organization improper practice, and the employer is joined as a party when the charge concerns a contract claim.
dfr_forum.quote: To breach its duty of fair representation. The public employer is made a party to any charge which alleges that the certified or recognized bargaining agent breached its duty of fair representation in the processing of or failure to process a claim that the public employer has breached the contract with the employee organization.
dfr_forum.pinpoint: PERB, What Is the Taylor Law?, part VI (employee organization improper practices)
